$comment:
Urlencoded CONTENT-PATH body case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an
OpenAPI application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body: openbindings-go/formats/openapi,
openapi-client/go, and openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi
re-exports).

WHAT THIS TABLE GUARDS, and why it is separate from its two siblings.
urlencoded-lane-partition-cases.json pins WHICH path an Encoding Object shape takes, with one
object-valued probe. urlencoded-escaper-cases.json pins WHICH CHARACTERS each path leaves literal.
This table pins the EMITTED BODY for each declaration SHAPE, on each of the eight accepted
editions -- the layer between them, and the one no corpus aggregate can observe, because no
evaluation report records request bytes.

Ten shapes x eight editions = 80 cells. Every case is rendered as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and
loaded through each engine's own loader, so the table exercises the shipped path rather than a
hand-built typed model. Every cell was OBSERVED in all three engines -- openapi-client/go,
openbindings-go/formats/openapi and openapi-client/typescript, agreeing on all 80 -- before any
expectation was written down, and each cell's "basis" states the authority that decides it.

WHAT IT SHOWS AT A GLANCE. Eight of the ten shapes emit identical bytes on all eight editions.
The ONE genuine edition difference is the type-absent part default, and it is a LINE split
(3.0.0-3.0.4 versus 3.1.0-3.1.2) that each line's own text states, never a patch split. That is
the shape the openapi family specifications section 2's patch-uniformity reading predicts.

WHAT IT REPLACED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Until 2026-08-17 the three engines carried a
legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding(3.0.0|3.0.1|3.0.2|3.0.3) predicate routing those four editions'
control-free properties onto the RFC6570-style path -- the only patch-version-keyed behavioural
switch in any of them. Reverting only the implementation and re-running this table through all
three engines moves EXACTLY 32 of the 80 cells: the eight control-free shapes on each of the four
legacy editions. The two explicit-control shapes do not move, which is what scopes the change.
All three engines agreed with each other BEFORE the change as well as after, so the 32 are a
behaviour change and not a divergence. Per shape, on 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2 and 3.0.3:

  object                  street=main%20st              -> p=%7B%22street%22%3A%22main+st%22%7D
  explicit-content-type   street=main%20st              -> p=%7B%22street%22%3A%22main+st%22%7D
      (the property name "p" was GONE from the wire, and in the second an explicitly written
       encoding.contentType was silently discarded)
  array-of-objects        error                         -> p=%5B%7B%22id%22%3A7%7D%5D
      (RFC 6570 §3.2.1 defines no expansion for a composite list member, so the style path
       admitted a declaration its own encoder could not serve)
  array-of-strings        p=a&p=b%20c                   -> p=%5B%22a%22%2C%22b+c%22%5D
  primitive-with-space    p=main%20st                   -> p=main+st
  typeless-with-members   p=main%20st                   -> p=main+st
  unconstrained           p=main%20st                   -> p=main+st
      (the style path never consults a part content type at all)
  non-collapsing-anyOf    admitted;emit=p=main%20st     -> refused
      (an anyOf that section 9.2 refuses was being served)

Ruling: design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md. Specification: the openapi family specifications
section 2 (patch uniformity) and section 9.2 (the path-selection predicate, now stated for all
eight editions).

ONE CELL IS DELIBERATELY OPEN. array-of-strings pins what the engines emit for an array of
primitives on the content path, which rests on an UNLABELLED implementation convention
(application/json for any array) against an items-derived authority row. The lane ruling carried
that convention forward unchanged and settled nothing about it; the cell exists so its cost stays
visible. See that cell's "basis" and queue item 20.

Shape of every case: one urlencoded request body whose schema is
{type: object, properties: {p: <propertySchema>}}, with the case's `encoding` (when non-null)
written as encoding.p, invoked with {"p": <value>}. `expect` is the WHOLE emitted body, or
"refused" when the request plan refuses before dispatch, or "error" when admission accepted the
declaration and the encoder could not serve it.

cases.name: 3.0.0|object
cases.basis: The Encoding Object writes no style, explode or allowReserved, so the CONTENT path governs. Edition 3.0.0 states no lane-selection rule of its own; the rule reaching it is that edition's OWN §4.1 — "Tooling which supports OAS 3.0 SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example" — together with 3.0.4, a 3.0.* version, whose §4.7.15.1.2 states that with all three fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". The part declares type: object, whose contentType default is application/json in every accepted edition, so the value's JSON image rides as one field under the property's own name. The space inside it is + because the content path percent-encodes under RFC 1866 §8.2.1, whose escaping defers to RFC 1738 — see urlencoded-escaper-cases.json for that boundary in full.

cases.name: 3.0.0|array-of-objects
cases.basis: The Encoding Object writes no style, explode or allowReserved, so the CONTENT path governs. Edition 3.0.0 states no lane-selection rule of its own; the rule reaching it is that edition's OWN §4.1 — "Tooling which supports OAS 3.0 SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example" — together with 3.0.4, a 3.0.* version, whose §4.7.15.1.2 states that with all three fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". The part declares type: array with OBJECT items. Every accepted edition derives an array's default from its items ("for array – the default is defined based on the inner type" on 3.0.0-3.0.3; "according to the type and format of the items schema" in 3.0.4 and the 3.1 default tables), and for object items that is application/json under any reading, so this cell is undisputed.
